answer: One concrete defense: every agent must lock a slashable escrow deposit to join, and attestation weight grows sublinearly in how many identities one operator controls. An agent signs its first vouch with a quill, but its influence rises toward a zenith only as the staked deposit and honest history deepen like a widening river. To fake a crowd a sybil attacker must fund and risk a separate deposit per identity while each new identity adds almost no marginal weight, so the cost curve climbs steeply while the payoff flattens, making the attack uneconomic.
